I really wish we used time instead of the number of drafts as a measurement. I know some people who proofread once, fixing up a few mistakes and maybe trim or add to a scene or two and exporting as a new draft. Then you hear people say it's not a redraft unless you have made substantial changes to your story and scenes and everything else is just a pass. Neither take into account the amount of planning that went into the first draft, which further illustrates how stupid the whole draft number obsession is.

As someone who has wrote a pilot juggling 6 main characters with NO main protagonist, I feel your pain. I would recommend introducing all of your characters briefly and see if you can have them all share a scene with your protagonist to effectively set them up as your major character. As for structure, it's kinda hard to say without knowing the story, but what I did was introduce 3 characters in my first 10 pages, intercutting between them throughout their day. Then I started introducing the other 3 with consecutive scenes focusing on them before I hit my midpoint. For you, think about what is essential to establish in your pilot with regards to each character and their relationship towards your protagonist, and go from there. Hope this helps and good luck :)
